title: Trainforge Chunk v4
description: Defines the per-chunk record emitted by Trainforge in chunks.jsonl and chunks.json. Each chunk is a retrieval-layer node in the course knowledge graph and carries text, HTML, source provenance, Bloom's level, and content-type metadata. Validation is enabled with TRAINFORGE_VALIDATE_CHUNKS=true.
$comment: The root permits additional properties so enrichment metadata can evolve without invalidating otherwise conformant chunks. The source object remains strict because it defines the structural provenance core. Shared taxonomy references keep classification values consistent across schemas.

id.description: Globally unique chunk identifier. Default form: '<course_slug>_chunk_<5-digit position>'. When TRAINFORGE_CONTENT_HASH_IDS=true, the suffix is the first 16 hexadecimal characters of the SHA-256 digest over text, source locator, and schema version, making IDs stable across re-chunks. Examples: example_course_chunk_00001 and example_course_chunk_a3f2b9c8d1e4f567.

schema_version.description: Chunk schema version literal. Downstream readers gate on this to dispatch parser versions without re-reading manifest.json.

chunk_type.description: Chunk content classification constrained by the shared content-type taxonomy.

text.description: Plain-text extraction used for retrieval. Post-canonicalize_sc_references (WCAG SC references collapsed to canonical form).

html.description: Original HTML fragment the chunk was derived from. Preserved for downstream rendering.

follows_chunk.description: ID of the immediately preceding chunk in the same module, or null for the first chunk.

concept_tags.description: Normalized concept slugs extracted from text + key terms (see process_course.py::_extract_concept_tags).

learning_outcome_refs.description: IDs of learning outcomes this chunk supports. Empty arrays permit content imported without learning-outcome references.

difficulty_provenance.description: Provenance tag for `difficulty` (honest IRT scaffold, gated by TRAINFORGE_IRT_DIFFICULTY_SCAFFOLD). 'heuristic' = the Bloom->difficulty / keyword cascade in _determine_difficulty; 'calibrated' = overridden from real learner responses via lib/assessment/irt_difficulty.py. Optional + hash-excluded; absent on legacy corpora and on every chunk when the scaffold flag is off (mirrors bloom_level_source).

difficulty_b.description: Rasch (1PL) difficulty from observed proportion-correct (b = ln((1-p)/p)); higher = harder. The only calibrated quantity.

discrimination_a.description: Fixed Rasch (1PL) discrimination convention value (1.0). NOT a fitted 2PL discrimination — the honest scaffold ships no 2PL fit.

n_responses.description: Number of real learner responses backing this calibration.

difficulty_irt.description: Honest IRT difficulty-calibration block (TRAINFORGE_IRT_DIFFICULTY_SCAFFOLD). Written ONLY when difficulty_provenance=='calibrated' with real backing responses; never fabricated for an item with no data. Optional + hash-excluded; absent on legacy corpora and on heuristic-provenance chunks.

bloom_level.description: Always populated. Resolution cascade (process_course.py:1099-1140): section JSON-LD > page JSON-LD > parsed LO > text verb heuristic > 'understand' default.

observed_bloom_level.description: Observed Bloom level classified for the chunk. It uses the same taxonomy as bloom_level and is populated when the source block supplies observedBloomLevel JSON-LD; null indicates that no observation is available.

bloom_alignment.description: Boolean alignment signal that is true when observed_bloom_level equals bloom_level. Null indicates that no classifier observation is available.

source_block_role.description: Semantic role of the source SemantiK region, such as 'body', 'figure', or 'heading'. Harvested from the data-semantik-block-role HTML attribute on the same opening tag as data-semantik-block-id. Optional when the source HTML provides no block role.

source_block_confidence.description: Classification confidence for the source SemantiK region, harvested from the data-semantik-confidence HTML attribute. Optional float in [0,1]; omission represents an unavailable value or the adapter's implicit full-confidence value.

wcag_block_status.description: Per-region WCAG gate verdict for the source SemantiK region, harvested from the data-semantik-wcag HTML attribute. Optional when the source HTML carries no block-level WCAG status.

figure_alt.description: Alt text or figcaption recovered from a figure chunk's

semantic_preservation_score.description: Document-level semantic-preservation score from the SemantiK result. The same value is attached to every chunk from a document and is recovered from the document sidecar rather than chunk HTML. Optional float in [0,1].

certification_status.description: SemantiK document certification status used for corpus-admission gating and WCAG auditing. The same value applies to every chunk from a document and is recovered from the document sidecar.

composite_unit.description: Composite pedagogical-unit type of the chunk's constituent sections, harvested from the SemantiK data-semantik-unit attribute. Uniform sections carry their shared type; mixed sections use the plurality type or null on a tie. Values come from the profile-extensible SemantiK lexicon, so the schema imposes no fixed enum.

unit_roles.description: Sorted, distinct pedagogical flow and opener role slugs present across the chunk's constituent sections. Values combine data-semantik-flow and data-semantik-opener roles from the profile-extensible SemantiK lexicon.

unit_subclass.description: Finer subclass of the resolved composite pedagogical unit, harvested from data-semantik-subclass on the unit section. A subclass is carried only when composite_unit resolves; chunks spanning tied unit types carry neither value. Labels are kebab-case and profile-extensible, so the schema imposes no fixed enum. Subclass metadata does not affect chunk text or identifiers.

bloom_level_source.description: Provenance tag for bloom_level. Only emitted when source is 'verbs' or 'default' (low-confidence paths), per process_course.py:1145.

bloom_level_secondary.description: Secondary, lower Bloom level when the source declares a compound bloom_level such as 'remember-apply'. The higher level becomes bloom_level while this field preserves the lower level without expanding the canonical taxonomy.

cognitive_task_type.description: Observable cognitive task such as classify, compute, debug, critique, explain, compare, or construct. This axis captures what the learner does independently of Bloom level or assessment format. Source-supplied values override text-based detection; the field is absent when no canonical task matches.

content_type_label.description: Free-form section or content classification label from JSON-LD or data-cf-content-type.

curies.description: CURIE tokens associated with the source block, combining data-cf-curie spans harvested before synthetic span text is removed with CURIEs already present in text. This is the authoritative source set for the curie_anchoring gate; consumers use text extraction when the field is absent.

forced_curies.description: Subset of `curies` whose source span carried data-cf-curie-forced="true" — i.e. the rewrite LLM dropped them and RewriteProvider._force_inject_curies stamped them back. A non-empty value is a rewrite-tier CURIE-preservation failure signal the curie_anchoring gate treats as a fail sub-signal. Subset-of-`curies` invariant (enforced by the validator, not the schema).

misconceptions.description: Per-chunk misconceptions normalized from page-level JSON-LD. Union permits dict (Courseforge-emitted) or plain string (non-Courseforge IMSCC passthrough); see process_course.py:1177-1184.

targeted_concepts.description: Bloom-qualified learning-outcome-to-concept bindings propagated from the chunk's cited learning outcomes. Each entry binds a canonical concept slug to the Bloom demand at which an outcome targets it. Values originate in learningObjectives[].targetedConcepts[], are normalized to snake_case, and are deduplicated by concept and bloom_level.

bloom_level.$comment: The inlined canonical BloomLevel enum mirrors concept_graph_semantic.schema.json $defs/TargetsConceptEvidence and avoids a cross-schema reference for this single field.

summary.description: Deterministic extractive summary from Trainforge/generators/summary_factory.py for dense-retrieval recall augmentation.

retrieval_text.description: summary + ' ' + key_terms_joined. Emitted only when key_terms present (benchmarked in Trainforge/rag/retrieval_benchmark.py).

_metadata_trace.description: Diagnostic mapping from each enrichment field to its source path. The schema permits this optional metadata so diagnostic chunk records remain valid.

key_claims.description: Per-block factual claims carried from Courseforge outline output. Structured entries may map each claim to specific SemantiK or Courseforge chunk IDs; the string-array form remains valid for compatibility. Independent claim entries are concatenated when small sections merge.

evidence_quote.description: Verbatim substring from a cited chunk's text that supports claim. Validation requires the quote to occur in at least one chunk named by source_chunk_ids. Null indicates that no grounded quote was emitted; the 240-character cap limits learning-outcome leakage.

evidence_char_span.description: Half-open [start, end) character offset of evidence_quote within the matched cited chunk's text. Validation requires chunk.text[start:end] to equal evidence_quote. Null when no grounded quote is available.

objective_alignment.description: Per-block, per-objective tri-axis delivery alignment carried from Courseforge validators. Each entry represents an objective the originating block claims to teach or assess. Merged sections deduplicate entries by objective_id using first-seen precedence.

learning_outcome_source_refs.description: Per-chunk reverse map from learning_outcome_refs to the SemantiK or Courseforge chunk IDs that source each learning outcome. Built from learningObjectives[].sourceReferences at emission time and omitted when the page-level JSON-LD declares no applicable references. Keys preserve their emitted case.

run_id.description: Identifier of the pipeline run that produced this chunk. It matches the decision-event run_id format and comes from the active DecisionCapture instance. Optional so existing chunk records remain valid.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp recorded when the chunk is emitted. Optional so existing chunk records remain valid.

source_pages.description: Sorted, deduplicated union of page numbers across the SemantiK blocks composing this chunk. It is top-level because Source is strict, and is omitted when no composing block supplies data-semantik-pages. It supports retrieval citations independently of minted source_references, while per-block pages remain available within source references.

Source.description: Chunk provenance block. course_id, module_id, and lesson_id form the required structural core; additionalProperties=false prevents silent drift. Audit fields support the Section 508 and ADA Title II round-trip contract, while source_references carries SemantiK and Courseforge provenance in the canonical source-reference shape.

module_title.description: Human-readable module title. Optional for non-Courseforge IMSCC imports that lack module naming.

section_heading.description: Heading of the section this chunk came from. May carry '(part N)' suffix for multi-part text blocks.

html_xpath.description: XPath into the source IMSCC HTML element (audit-trail; enables element_text = resolve_xpath(raw_html, html_xpath)).

char_span.description: [start, end] character offset range within the xpath-resolved element.

item_path.description: IMSCC-relative path to the source HTML file, for auditor navigation without imsmanifest.xml traversal.

source_document_sha256.description: SHA-256 digest of the upstream source document, either the SemantiK HTML aggregate or IMSCC archive. The value matches the corresponding sidecar manifest digest and is constant across chunks from the same source, providing a byte-stable lineage join key. It is optional for compatibility and propagates into concept-graph and LibV2 manifest lineage fields.

source_references.description: SemantiK and Courseforge source references collected from JSON-LD sourceReferences and data-cf-source-ids attributes. The array supports chunks merged from multiple sections. Absence means provenance is unknown; merged references use primary, contributing, then corroborating role precedence.

Misconception.description: A correction is required, together with at least one of misconception or its statement alias. Optional Bloom and cognitive-domain metadata is normalized from JSON-LD camelCase to snake_case by the HTML content parser.

statement.description: Alias for misconception with equivalent semantics.

bloom_level.description: Bloom's taxonomy level targeted by this misconception. Courseforge infers it from the correction or misconception statement, while source-supplied values take precedence.

cognitive_domain.description: Cognitive domain derived from bloom_level and emitted only when bloom_level is populated.

cognitive_task_type.description: Observable cognitive task such as classify, compute, debug, or critique. This axis captures what the learner does independently of Bloom level. It is populated when the correction or statement contains a canonical task verb, with JSON-LD camelCase normalized to snake_case.

id.description: Canonical misconception ID minted by lib/ontology/misconception_id.py::canonical_mc_id over (misconception, correction, bloom_level). Read by Trainforge/generators/staged/micro.py::micro_preference_eligibility, which REJECTS the entry when a supplied ID disagrees with the recomputed canonical one. Optional — omit it and the canonical ID is derived. Permitted here because additionalProperties is false and the eligibility arm already reads this key; without it a provenance-carrying misconception was unrepresentable.

mechanism_evidence.description: Source-grounded evidence explaining WHY the misconception is wrong — the DPO rejected-branch justification. Read by micro_preference_eligibility, which falls back to error_mechanism and then to 'correction' when absent. Optional.

error_mechanism.description: Alias for mechanism_evidence, read second in the same fallback chain. Optional.

source_block_id.description: Authored block instance the misconception came from, shape {page_id}#{block_type}_{slug}_{idx}. Preserves per-block provenance through to the emitted preference pair; micro_preference_eligibility falls back to the chunk ID when absent. Optional.
